title: regional-data-incident-communication-runbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This doc is a working runbook for how we communicate internally and to customers when a data residency or regional pinning incident occurs (misrouted traffic, temporary fallback to non-resident region, storage boundary breach, mis-applied pin). It covers: detection signals, initial triage, immediate containment actions, internal notifications, legal & compliance escalation, customer-facing messaging templates, telemetry/evidence collection, and post-incident follow-up.

Audience:
- Oncall engineers (residency, routing, serving runtime)
- SRE and Platform incident commanders
- Legal / Privacy / Security leads
- CS/Account leads for affected customers
- Product owner for Private deployments

Principles (quick):
- Safety first: contain cross-border exposures before detailed root-cause analysis.
- Be honest but measured in external comms (avoid speculation).
- Gather audit-grade evidence for legal/compliance review.
- Use customer segmentation: high-risk customers (regulated industries) get faster, tailored comms.

Detection signals (automated + human):
- Telemetry anomalies:
  - sudden spike in regional routing failures or fallback-to-global route metric (route.fallback.count > baseline by 5x)
  - mismatch in request.region header vs. serving-region tag on response
  - KV cache writes occurring in non-pinned region for pinned account
  - storage put events to non-resident bucket (S3 put events with org-id tag mismatch)
- Alerts from customer: support tickets, CS escalation
- Audit job findings: nightly residency audit detects pin violations
- Manual report from operators during maintenance or deploys

Triage checklist (first 30 minutes):
1) Acknowledge and classify incident severity (S1/S2/S3):
   - S1: confirmed cross-border exposure of customer data (PII or regulated) or production-wide misrouting
   - S2: potential exposure (inconclusive telemetry) or single-customer misroute not yet confirmed
   - S3: config-only anomaly with no data movement
2) Assign Incident Lead (IL) and Communications Lead (CL) — usually from SRE and CS respectively. Put both in incident Slack channel (#inc-residency-<shortid>).
3) Capture initial facts: time window, affected customers/org IDs, impacted regions, approximate request count, whether persistent storage was involved.
4) If S1 or storage involved -> page Legal & Security immediately.
5) Implement containment:
   - Remove/disable misrouting policy or revert the suspicious routing change (rollback on PR or flip feature flag).
   - For pinned accounts, force immediate reroute to pinned endpoint via emergency ACL if available.
   - If data landed in wrong bucket, snapshot bucket and enable object-lock/read-only to preserve evidence.
6) Create Jira incident (use INC prefix) and link to Slack channel and this doc.

Roles & responsibilities (quick reference):
- Incident Lead (IL): triage, make containment decisions, coordinate engineers.
- Communications Lead (CL): drafts customer messages, syncs with Legal and CS.
- Legal/Privacy: reviews external comms and informs regulatory obligations (notifiers, timelines).
- Customer Success / Account Rep: direct customer contact, tailored messaging.
- SRE/Platform Engineers: telemetry queries, rollback, infrastructure containment.
- Serving-runtime Eng: fix model routing, cache invalidation, quantization/eviction checks.

Immediate evidence collection (must be done before any destructive actions):
- Snapshot routing tables and change history (control-plane events).
- Export logs for affected time window: ingress logs, routing logs, storage events, KV writes.
- Preserve S3/GCS objects that may contain copied data.
- Export per-request headers showing region tags.
- Take screenshots of operator consoles/PR diff if config change suspected.
- Note: do NOT purge evidence even if it contains sensitive data — Legal needs full chain.

Customer communication templates (first-notice sample) - short and conservative:
Subject: Important: Temporary routing anomaly affecting regional data placement

Body (first-notice):
Hi <CustomerName> team,

We want to let you know we detected an anomaly where a subset of requests for your org (ID <org-id>) may have been routed outside your designated region between <start time> and <end time>. We are actively investigating and have taken steps to contain the issue. At this stage we do not have evidence of unauthorized access; we are preserving logs and data for a full investigation.

What we are doing now:
- Contained routing change and prevented further cross-region writes
- Preserved logs and storage for forensic review
- Engaging our legal and security teams to evaluate impact and next steps

We will follow up within 24 hours with findings and remediation steps. If you have immediate questions, please reply or contact your account lead, <AE name>.

Sincerely,
Redwood Inference Support

Customer follow-up (24-hour): update with: confirmed scope (requests, storage objects), remediation (data deletion, re-ingest, re-pinning), any regulatory notifications initiated, timeline for full post-mortem.

Regulatory/legal checklist (to be completed by Legal):
- Is this a notifiable event under GDPR/UK DPA/PDPA/other? If yes, timeline for regulator notification (72 hours for GDPR from breach discovery).
- Identify affected personal data categories and number of subjects.
- Assess contract SLA/DPAs to determine contractual notices to customers.
- Determine whether customer-driven mitigation (e.g., reingest in correct region) is needed and who bears cost.

Operational playbook for containment (specific commands / ops actions - examples):
- Roll back routing PR: git repo redwood-routing, revert PR #<id> and restart control-plane service.
- Force pinned routing: curl -XPOST https://ops.internal/routing/force-route -d '{"org": "<org-id>", "region": "eu-west-1"}' (ops-only endpoint)
- Snapshot S3: aws s3api put-object-lock-configuration --bucket <bucket> --object-lock-enabled-for-bucket -- ...
- KV cache eviction: call maintenance API to invalidate KV namespaces for <org-id> across regional caches.

Telemetry queries (useful snippets):
- Count of requests by serving-region and org-id: SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE org = '<org-id>' AND served_region != pinned_region AND ts BETWEEN '<start>' AND '<end>';
- Storage put events to non-resident buckets: filter storage_events where bucket.region != org.pinned_region
- Top callers by IP/user agent during window (for suspicious access correlation)

Decision matrix for external notification severity:
- Notify customers only (no regulator): possible exposure limited, only non-sensitive metadata, or confirmed no regulated data -> customer email + status-page update.
- Notify regulator + customers: confirmed PII/reg data in wrong region, or cross-border copy persisted to storage.
- Emergency public statement: material outage with broad customer impact or legally required disclosure.

Status page and public comms guidelines:
- Use status.redwood.io: create incident with 'data residency' tag; update with minimal factual timeline and expected next update time. Avoid technical blame.

Post-incident actions (72 hours & follow-up):
- Full RCA draft within 72 hours with scope, root cause, remediation, and impact matrix (per-customer).
- Long-term mitigation plan: policy enforcement automation, stronger pre-merge checks, expanded residency unit tests in CI, control-plane change gating for residency-affecting PRs.
- Compensation / remediation proposals for impacted customers (credit, free private-deploy run for re-ingest, engineering support).
- Update residency audit jobs and run full audit across all pinned accounts.

Templates & snippets (placeholders for quick copy):
- Slack alert format: [INC-<id>] Residency anomaly: org:<org-id> suspected misroute to <region>. IL: @<name>, CL:@<name>. Containment: in progress. Evidence stored: s3://redwood-audit/..
- Jira summary: INC-<id> Residency misroute for org <org-id> -> <from-region> to <to-region> (count: <n>)

Open questions / items to decide (notes to self):
- Do we have an automated short-circuit that instantly forces re-pin for accounts with very strict DPAs? If not, add feature ticket.
- Should we create a per-org webhook to notify customers when any residency-related change occurs? PQ for product.
- How do we balance object-lock preservation (evidence) vs customer request to delete inadvertently copied data quickly? Legal to own SLA for that decision.

Appendix: quick contacts
- Legal: privacy@redwood.com (paging oncall: legal-oncall@pagerduty)
- Security: sec-ops@redwood.com (slack #sec-ops)
- CS escalation: cs-escalation@redwood.com
- Oncall (residency): rota-residency@redwood.com (pagerduty)

Revision notes:
- 2024-09-18: initial draft by Maya Lopez
- 2024-11-02: added telemetry queries and evidence checklist (Arjun)
- 2025-02-12: added customer templates and regulatory checklist (Sophie)
